concepts.title: Major Nutrients in Food
concepts.definition: Essential substances contained in food that nourish the body, build structures, provide energy, and sustain biological functions.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Dietary food comprises five primary nutrient groups along with fibre and water.
question_patterns: what are the major nutrients present in our food
list the essential components required by the human body
name the five main classes of dietary nutrients
which substances in food support life and growth

solution_steps.explain: The main nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals.
Dietary fibre (roughage) and water are essential additions to daily intake.

concepts.title: Test for Starch
concepts.definition: A chemical procedure where dilute iodine solution is added to a food sample to detect complex carbohydrates through color change.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A dark blue-black color change confirms the presence of starch.
question_patterns: how do you test for the presence of starch in a food item
describe the iodine test for carbohydrates
what color indicates a positive result for starch test
calculate or identify the reaction result when iodine hits potato sample

solution_steps.explain: Place a small portion of raw or cooked food item in a container.
Add 2 to 3 drops of diluted iodine solution onto the food sample.
A blue-black tint confirms the presence of starch.

concepts.title: Test for Proteins
concepts.definition: In brief, a biochemical test where aqueous copper both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both sulphate and caustic soda solutions react with proteins to yield a violet solution.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Formation of a distinct violet color indicates protein content.
question_patterns: how can you test a food sample for protein presence
what chemicals are used to detect protein in food items
describe the chemical steps of testing groundnut or egg for proteins
what color change confirms proteins during chemical testing

solution_steps.explain: Grind food sample into fine powder/paste and mix with 10 drops of water in a test tube.
Dispense 2 drops of copper sulphate solution followed by 10 drops of caustic soda solution.
Mix and allow to stand; a violet color verifies protein presence.

concepts.title: Test for Fats
concepts.definition: A physical test where food is pressed on paper to leave a translucent greasy spot that remains visible after drying.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A persistent oily mark on paper demonstrates lipid content.
question_patterns: how do you test a food item for fat content
describe the paper spot test for lipids
how to differentiate oily patches from water spots on paper
what observation indicates that a food contains fat

solution_steps.explain: Enclose food item in paper and crush gently without rupturing the sheet.
Unfold paper and allow time for any water moisture to evaporate.
Hold paper to light; a translucent greasy spot confirms presence of fat.

concepts.title: Carbohydrates and Fats as Energy Sources
concepts.definition: Nutrient categories that undergo cellular respiration to generate biological fuel, with lipids providing higher caloric yield per mass.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, both both both both both both both both both both both both Fats and carbohydrates supply bodily energy, with fats yielding significantly more.
question_patterns: which nutrients are called energy giving foods
compare energy output from equal amounts of fat and carbohydrate
why does the body require carbohydrates and fats
which nutrient group provides maximum energy to humans

solution_steps.explain: Carbohydrates and fats act as fuel for cellular metabolic processes.
Gram for gram, fats provide roughly double the energy supplied by carbohydrates.

concepts.title: Functions of Dietary Proteins
concepts.definition: Structural biological molecules essential for tissue construction, cellular repair, and physical growth of the body.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Proteins are body-building nutrients vital for both growth and tissue renewal.
question_patterns: why are proteins called body building foods
what biological roles do proteins perform in humans
which nutrient is necessary for repairing broken tissue and muscle growth
name plant and animal sources rich in proteins

solution_steps.explain: Proteins synthesize structural components required for cellular growth and tissue repair.
Foods high in protein are grouped under body-building nutrition.

concepts.title: Functions of Vitamins and Minerals
concepts.definition: Micronutrients required in trace quantities to safeguard against physiological disorders and support skeletal and systemic health.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, both both both both both both both both both both both both Vitamins and minerals act as protective nutrients maintaining immune defense and metabolic balance.
question_patterns: why are vitamins referred to as protective foods
what is the role of Vitamin A, C, and D in human health
which mineral is required for strong teeth and bones
how does iron or iodine contribute to human metabolic health

solution_steps.explain: Vitamin A maintains skin and vision, Vitamin C aids immune defense, Vitamin D enables calcium uptake.
Calcium hardens bone matrix, Iron produces blood hemoglobin, Iodine enables thyroid gland synthesis.

concepts.title: Role of Roughage and Water
concepts.definition: Non-caloric food components consisting of indigestible plant fibers and liquid solvent necessary for digestion and excretion.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Roughage prevents constipation while water dissolves nutrients and removes body wastes.
question_patterns: what is dietary fibre or roughage and why is it necessary
how does water assist in body metabolic functions
why must we consume dietary components that provide no nutrients
which food items supply maximum dietary fiber

solution_steps.explain: Dietary fibre adds bulk to digestive waste, enabling efficient movement through intestines.
Water acts as a solvent for nutrient absorption and flushes waste out through sweat and urine.

concepts.title: Balanced Diet and Preservation of Nutrients
concepts.definition: A meal plan delivering all essential dietary components in appropriate proportions while employing proper cooking to prevent nutrient destruction.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, a balanced meal covers all nutritional requirements without excess calorie or nutrient loss during preparation.
question_patterns: what constitutes a balanced diet
how does improper cooking or excessive washing reduce nutritional value
why should fruits and vegetables not be washed after peeling
which vitamin gets destroyed easily by heat during cooking

solution_steps.explain: Incorporate suitable quantities of energy foods, proteins, vitamins, minerals, roughage, and water.
Avoid repetitive washing of peeled produce and excessive heating, which degrades water-soluble vitamins like Vitamin C.

concepts.title: Nutrient Deficiency Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological conditions arising in an organism due to long-term insufficient intake of specific dietary nutrients.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Prolonged omission of key vitamins or minerals causes specific clinical disorders preventable by a balanced diet.
question_patterns: what are deficiency diseases
which disease is caused by lack of Vitamin D or Vitamin C
identify symptoms of goitre, scurvy, or beriberi
how can deficiency disorders be prevented

solution_steps.explain: Disorders resulting from sustained lack of particular nutrients over long periods.
Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; B1 causes Beriberi; C causes Scurvy; D causes Rickets; Calcium causes tooth/bone decay; Iodine causes Goitre; Iron causes Anemia.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student added drops of iodine solution to a slice of raw {food_item}. The slice turned blue-black. What nutrient is present?

solution_template.explain: Iodine solution interacting with a sample yields a blue-black color specifically in the presence of starch.
The blue-black reaction confirms that the raw potato contains starch (carbohydrates).

worked_examples.question_pattern: A child presents with soft and bent leg bones. Name the deficiency disease and missing {nutrient}.

solution_template.explain: Softened, weak, and bowed leg bones are characteristic symptoms of rickets.
Rickets is caused by a long-term dietary deficiency of Vitamin D.
